examples.ko: 출장비 신청서에 부장님 결재가 아직 안 났어요.
examples.en: The department head hasn't signed off on the travel expense form yet.

examples.ko: 출장비는 회사가 전액 부담하니까 영수증만 꼭 챙기세요.
examples.en: The company covers the travel expenses in full, so just be sure to keep your receipts.
The travel expenses this time came to more than I expected.

examples.ko: 출장비를 먼저 받고 나중에 정산해도 돼요?
examples.en: Can I receive the travel allowance first and settle up later?
Lodging and transportation are both included in the travel expenses.

examples.ko: 지난달 출장비 정산은 언제까지 해야 해요?
examples.en: By when do I have to settle last month's travel expenses?

explain: 회사 일로 다른 곳에 갈 때 쓰는 돈이라서 '출장비를 받다', '출장비를 정산하다'처럼 자주 말해요. 개인 여행에는 쓰지 않고, 보통 교통비·숙박비·식비가 함께 들어가요.
explain_en: It is the money for a business trip, so people say '출장비를 받다' (receive it) or '출장비를 정산하다' (settle it). It is not used for personal trips, and it usually covers transport, lodging and meals together.

examples.en: The stairs are narrow and steep, so you have to be careful.
The elevator was broken, so I went up by the stairs.
Kids are playing at the bottom of the stairs.
I came down those stairs slowly, one step at a time.
I left my umbrella at the end of the stairs.

examples.ko: 이 건물 층계는 폭이 넓어서 안전해요.
examples.en: The stairs in this building are wide, so they are safe.

explain: '계단'과 거의 같아서 바꿔 써도 돼요. 다만 '층계'는 조금 글 같은 느낌이 있어서, 대화에서는 '계단'이라고 말하는 사람이 많아요. '층계를 오르다/내려오다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '계단', so you can swap them. '층계' feels a bit more literary, and many people say '계단' in conversation. You say '층계를 오르다' (go up) or '층계를 내려오다' (come down).

examples.en: How many floors does this building have?
The higher the floor, the better the view.

examples.ko: 집을 구할 때 층수도 꼭 확인해요.
examples.en: When I look for a home, I always check the floor number too.
If the floor is low, it can be noisy.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터 안의 층수 표시가 고장 났어요.
examples.en: The floor indicator inside the elevator is broken.

examples.ko: 저는 너무 높지 않은 층수를 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like a floor that is not too high.

explain: '몇 층이에요?'는 한 층을 묻고, '층수'는 건물이 몇 층인지나 집이 몇 층인지를 숫자로 이야기할 때 써요. '층수가 높다/낮다'처럼 말하고, 집을 구할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '몇 층이에요?' asks about one floor, while '층수' is used when talking about floor numbers, either how tall a building is or which floor a home is on. You say '층수가 높다/낮다' (the floor is high/low), and it comes up a lot when looking for a home.

examples.en: The treatment room is at the end of the hall on the right.
I went to the treatment room for physical therapy.
Please be quiet inside the treatment room.

examples.ko: 치료실이 넓어서 침대가 여러 개 있어요.
examples.en: The treatment room is large, so it has several beds.
After the checkup, I got an injection in the treatment room.
The nurse showed me to the treatment room.

explain: 병원에서 의사가 진찰하는 곳은 '진료실', 주사나 물리 치료처럼 치료를 하는 곳은 '치료실'이라고 구분해서 말해요. 병원 안내판에서도 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: In a hospital, the place where the doctor examines you is the '진료실', and the place for injections or physical therapy is the '치료실'. You will often see both on hospital signs.

examples.ko: 친부모를 찾고 싶어서 입양 기관에 문의했어요.
examples.en: I wanted to find my biological parents, so I contacted an adoption agency.
My adoptive parents loved me as much as my biological parents would have.
It has been a long time since I lost contact with my biological parents.
You have to write your biological parents' names on the form.
I still don't know who my biological parents are.
My younger sibling grew up beside the biological parents.

explain: 입양이나 재혼 이야기에서 낳아 준 부모를 말할 때 써요. 짝말은 '양부모'(입양한 부모)이고, 높여서 말하면 '친부모님'이에요. 일반 대화에서 그냥 '부모님'이라고 하면 이런 구분이 없어요.
explain_en: It is used in talk about adoption or remarriage to mean the parents who gave birth to you. The opposite is '양부모' (adoptive parents), and the polite form is '친부모님'. In normal conversation, plain '부모님' carries no such distinction.

examples.en: I am going to see my mother this weekend.
My mother sent me some kimchi.
After I had the baby, my mother helped me a lot.
My mother farms in our hometown.
It is my mother's birthday, so I bought a gift.
I went to the market with my mother.

explain: 결혼한 여자가 자기 어머니를 시댁과 구분해서 말할 때 써요. 짝말은 '시어머니'(남편의 어머니)예요. 남편이 아내의 어머니를 말할 때는 '장모님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A married woman uses it to talk about her own mother as distinct from her husband's family. The counterpart is '시어머니' (husband's mother). A husband calls his wife's mother '장모님'.

examples.en: I played card games with my family during the holiday.
Card games have simple rules, so you learn them quickly.
My friends are totally hooked on card games.

examples.ko: 카드놀이 하다가 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I was playing cards and lost track of time.

examples.ko: 카드놀이로 내기를 하면 항상 제가 져요.
examples.en: When we bet on card games, I always lose.

examples.ko: 카드놀이가 재미있어서 여행 갈 때도 카드를 가져가요.
examples.en: Card games are fun, so I bring cards when I travel too.

explain: 트럼프 카드로 하는 놀이를 말해요. 화투로 하는 '고스톱'은 따로 부르고, '카드놀이'라고 하면 보통 트럼프 카드를 떠올려요.
explain_en: It refers to games played with a deck of playing cards. Games played with 화투 flower cards, like '고스톱', are named separately, and '카드놀이' usually makes people think of regular playing cards.

examples.en: The tire was flat, so I went to the car repair shop.
I got the engine oil changed at the garage.

examples.ko: 이 근처에 믿을 만한 카센터가 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a trustworthy car repair shop near here?

examples.ko: 카센터 사장님이 차를 꼼꼼히 봐 주셨어요.
examples.en: The owner of the repair shop checked my car carefully.
The garage is closed on Sundays.

examples.ko: 차에서 이상한 소리가 나서 카센터로 가져갔어요.
examples.en: The car was making a strange noise, so I took it to the garage.

explain: 자동차를 고치거나 점검하는 가게를 말하는 한국식 영어예요. 영어권에서는 'car center'가 아니라 'repair shop'이나 'garage'라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '정비소'가 있어요.
explain_en: This is Korean-style English for a shop that repairs or inspects cars. In English-speaking countries people say 'repair shop' or 'garage', not 'car center'. A similar Korean word is '정비소'.

examples.en: Castella is soft and sweet, so kids like it.
I had castella and milk for breakfast.

examples.ko: 이 집 카스텔라가 촉촉해서 정말 맛있어요.
examples.en: This shop's castella is moist and really delicious.

examples.ko: 커피랑 같이 카스텔라 한 조각만 주세요.
examples.en: Please give me just one slice of castella with a coffee.
I want to try baking castella at home.
This morning I spread strawberry jam on my castella and ate it.

explain: 표준 표기는 '카스텔라'지만 말할 때는 '카스테라'라고 하는 사람도 있어요. 빵집이나 편의점 빵 코너에서 흔히 보여요. 자를 때는 '한 조각', '한 쪽'으로 세요.
explain_en: The standard spelling is '카스텔라', but some people say '카스테라' in speech. You often see it in bakeries and convenience-store bread sections. When you cut it, you count pieces as '한 조각' or '한 쪽'.

en: to cut with a knife; to slice

examples.en: The chef chops quickly on the cutting board.
Don't chop the onion too big.
Even the way that chef handles a knife is different.
I almost cut my hand while chopping vegetables.

examples.ko: 손목에 힘을 빼고 칼질하면 덜 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you relax your wrist when you cut, it is less tiring.

examples.ko: 스테이크를 칼질할 때는 포크로 고기를 잡아요.
examples.en: When you cut a steak, you hold the meat with a fork.

explain: '썰다'는 재료를 자른다는 데 초점이 있고, '칼질하다'는 칼을 쓰는 동작이나 솜씨에 초점이 있어요. 그래서 '칼질이 빠르다', '칼질이 능숙하다'처럼 솜씨를 말할 때도 잘 써요.

phrases.en: It's our anniversary today, so let's go out for a steak dinner!
phrases.nuance_ko: 스테이크나 돈가스처럼 칼로 썰어 먹는 서양식 식사를 하러 간다는 말로, 편한 대화에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In casual talk it means going out for a Western-style meal, such as steak or pork cutlet, that you cut with a knife.
phrases.en_equiv: go out for a steak dinner

explain_en: '썰다' focuses on cutting the ingredient, while '칼질하다' focuses on the action of using the knife and the skill involved. That is why people also say '칼질이 빠르다' (quick with a knife) or '칼질이 능숙하다' (skilled with a knife).

examples.en: One caramel-flavored ice cream, please.
The caramel sticks to my teeth, so it's hard to eat.
Please add caramel syrup to my coffee.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 캐러멜을 먹다가 이가 빠졌어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my tooth came out while I was eating caramel.
This pudding tastes sweet like caramel.
Caramel is too sweet, so I only eat a little.

explain: '카라멜'이라고 쓰는 사람도 있지만 표준 표기는 '캐러멜'이에요. 씹어 먹는 사탕뿐 아니라 설탕을 녹여 만든 소스나 시럽 맛을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: Some people write '카라멜', but the standard spelling is '캐러멜'. It refers not only to the chewy candy but also to the flavor of sauces and syrups made from melted sugar.

examples.ko: 시험 시간에 커닝은 절대 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must never cheat during an exam.

examples.ko: 시험 중에 커닝을 하다가 들켜서 영점을 받았대요.
examples.en: I heard he was caught cheating during the exam and got a zero.
My friend got scolded by the teacher because of cheating.
Cheating is impossible on this test.
I got caught making a cheat sheet.

examples.ko: 우리 반에서 커닝으로 걸린 사람이 없어요.
examples.en: No one in our class has been caught cheating.

explain: 시험에서 몰래 답을 보는 행동만 말하고, 게임이나 연애에서 속이는 것에는 쓰지 않아요. '부정행위'는 공식적인 말이고, 학교에서는 '커닝'이라고 말해요. '커닝 페이퍼'는 몰래 보려고 적어 둔 쪽지예요.
explain_en: It only means secretly looking at answers on a test, and is not used for cheating in games or relationships. '부정행위' is the formal term, while at school people say '커닝'. A '커닝 페이퍼' is a cheat sheet written to peek at secretly.

examples.en: You must not cheat during the exam.

examples.ko: 옆 친구 답을 커닝하다가 선생님께 걸렸어요.
examples.en: I got caught by the teacher copying my neighbor's answers.

examples.ko: 저는 한 번도 커닝해 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never cheated even once.
Don't cheat; try to solve it on your own.
Nobody knows who cheated.

examples.ko: 시험 감독 선생님이 커닝하는 학생을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The proctor is looking for students who are cheating.

explain: '컨닝'이라고 잘못 쓰는 경우가 많은데 표준 표기는 '커닝'이에요. 시험에서 몰래 답을 보는 것에만 쓰고, 공식 문서에서는 '부정행위를 하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Many people misspell it as '컨닝', but the standard spelling is '커닝'. It is used only for secretly looking at answers in a test, and formal documents say '부정행위를 하다' instead.

en: electric kettle (in Korean usage); coffee pot

examples.en: I boil water in the kettle and drink tea.
The kettle broke, so I bought a new one.
The kettle in the office is always on.
I boiled water for ramen in the kettle.
You have to wipe the inside of the kettle clean.

examples.ko: 커피포트를 쓴 뒤에는 전원을 꼭 뽑으세요.
examples.en: After using the kettle, be sure to unplug it.

explain: 한국에서 '커피포트'는 물을 끓이는 전기 주전자를 가리킬 때가 많아서, 커피를 내리는 기계로 알면 헷갈려요. 커피를 내리는 기계는 '커피 머신'이나 '커피메이커'라고 해요.
explain_en: In Korea '커피포트' often means an electric kettle for boiling water, so thinking of it as a coffee-brewing machine can be confusing. A machine that brews coffee is called a '커피 머신' or '커피메이커'.

examples.en: I caught a head cold and my nose keeps running.
My head cold is bad, so I can't smell anything.
I get a stuffy-nose cold whenever the seasons change.
My voice sounds strange because of my cold.
A head cold gets better after a few days of rest.
I took cold medicine last night, and now I'm sleepy.

explain: 콧물과 코막힘이 중심인 감기를 말해요. 목이 아픈 감기는 '목감기'라고 해서 증상에 따라 나눠 부르기도 해요. 보통 '코감기에 걸리다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It means a cold whose main symptoms are a runny or blocked nose. A cold with a sore throat is called '목감기', so people sometimes name colds by their symptoms. You usually say '코감기에 걸리다'.

examples.en: The eldest son's wife has a lot to do during the holidays.
The eldest son's wife in our family is a good cook.
Grandmother trusts her eldest daughter-in-law the most.
She married in as the eldest son's wife and held the ancestral rites.
The whole family gathered for the eldest daughter-in-law's birthday.
The eldest and younger daughters-in-law get along well.

explain: 큰아들의 아내를 말하고, 짝말은 '작은며느리'(또는 '둘째 며느리')예요. 전통적으로 제사와 명절 일을 많이 맡는 자리라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It means the eldest son's wife, and the counterpart is '작은며느리' (or '둘째 며느리' for the second). Traditionally it carries a sense of the person who takes on much of the ancestral rites and holiday work.

examples.en: My eldest is starting university this year.
My eldest takes good care of her younger sibling.
I gave my eldest a little pocket money.
My older and younger kids fight often.

examples.ko: 큰애 학교 때문에 이사를 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to move because of my eldest's school.
I have to go to the school to pick up my eldest.

explain: 부모가 맏이 자녀를 말할 때 쓰고, 아들이든 딸이든 상관없어요. 짝말은 '작은애'이고, 형제가 셋 이상이면 '둘째', '막내'를 써요. '첫째'와 비슷하지만 '큰애'가 더 구어체예요.
explain_en: Parents use it for their eldest child, whether a son or a daughter. The counterpart is '작은애', and with three or more children you use '둘째' and '막내'. It is similar to '첫째' but more conversational.

examples.en: The ping-pong ball rolled under the table.
A ping-pong ball is light and small, so it bounces well.
If you hit the ping-pong ball hard, it flies far.

examples.ko: 새 탁구공 세 개만 사다 주세요.
examples.en: Please buy me just three new ping-pong balls.
I wrote my name on my ping-pong ball.
A bump the size of a ping-pong ball appeared on my forehead.

explain: '탁구공만 한'처럼 크기를 비교하는 말에 자주 나와요. 같은 방식으로 '주먹만 한', '콩알만 한'도 써요. 공은 '한 개, 두 개'로 세요.
explain_en: It often appears in size comparisons like '탁구공만 한' (as big as a ping-pong ball). The same pattern works with '주먹만 한' (fist-sized) and '콩알만 한' (bean-sized). You count balls as '한 개, 두 개'.

examples.ko: 국내선 탑승구가 어디예요? — 이 층 오른쪽에 있어요.
examples.en: Where is the domestic flight gate? — It's on this floor, on the right.

examples.ko: 탑승구가 바뀌었으니 안내 방송을 잘 들으세요.
examples.en: The gate has changed, so listen carefully to the announcements.

examples.ko: 비행기 출발 삼십 분 전에 탑승구에 도착하세요.
examples.en: Please arrive at the boarding gate thirty minutes before departure.
I'm waiting for my family in front of the gate.

examples.ko: 저쪽 탑승구는 아직 문이 닫혀 있어요.
examples.en: The gate over there is still closed.
It takes about ten minutes to walk to the gate.

explain: 공항에서 비행기에 타는 문이에요. 번호를 붙여 '십이 번 탑승구'처럼 말하고, 공항에서는 '게이트'라고 말하는 경우도 있어요.
explain_en: It is the door at the airport where you board the plane. You attach a number, as in '십이 번 탑승구' (gate 12), and at airports people sometimes just say '게이트'.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 털모자를 쓰면 귀가 안 시려요.
examples.en: If you wear a woolen hat in winter, your ears won't get cold.

examples.ko: 이건 할머니가 손수 짜 주신 털모자예요.
examples.en: This is a woolen hat my grandmother knitted by hand for me.
The woolen hat is big, so it keeps slipping down.
It's snowing, so wear a woolen hat when you go out.

examples.ko: 털모자는 세탁기에 돌리면 줄어들 수 있어요.
examples.en: A woolen hat can shrink if you put it in the washing machine.
The red woolen hat has a pom-pom on it.

explain: 모자는 '쓰다'를 쓰니까 '털모자를 쓰다'라고 해요. 털실로 짠 모자는 '니트 모자'나 '비니'라고도 해요. 짝으로 '털장갑', '목도리'가 같이 나와요.
explain_en: Hats take the verb '쓰다', so you say '털모자를 쓰다'. A hat knitted from wool yarn may also be called a '니트 모자' or '비니'. It is often paired with '털장갑' and '목도리' (scarf).

examples.en: My hands are warm because I put on woolen gloves.
I lost one of my woolen gloves.

examples.ko: 털장갑이 작아서 아이 손에 안 들어가요.
examples.en: The woolen gloves are small and don't fit on the child's hands.
I chose red for my new woolen gloves.

examples.ko: 털장갑 낀 채로 휴대폰을 하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: It's hard to use a phone with woolen gloves on.
Snow got on the woolen gloves and they got wet.

explain: 장갑은 손가락 부분에 '끼다'를 써서 '장갑을 끼다'라고 해요. 한 짝씩 '한 짝, 두 짝'으로 세고, 한 쌍은 '한 켤레'라고도 해요. 모자는 '쓰다', 목도리는 '하다/두르다'로 구분해요.
explain_en: Gloves take the verb '끼다', as in '장갑을 끼다'. You count single gloves as '한 짝, 두 짝', and a pair can be '한 켤레'. Hats use '쓰다' and scarves use '하다' or '두르다'.

en: born in the year of the rabbit

examples.en: I was born in the year of the rabbit. What's your zodiac sign?

examples.ko: 토끼띠는 열두 띠 중에 네 번째예요.
examples.en: The rabbit is the fourth of the twelve zodiac animals.
My older brother is a rabbit and I'm a dragon.
I heard the people born in the year of the rabbit started a group.

examples.ko: 이번 모임에는 토끼띠가 세 명이나 왔어요.
examples.en: Three people born in the year of the rabbit came to this gathering.
My mother was born in the year of the rabbit, so she collects rabbit dolls.

explain: 한국에서는 나이를 직접 묻기 어려울 때 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 돌려 묻기도 해요. 같은 띠인 사람끼리는 열두 살씩 차이가 나요. '띠'는 앞에 동물 이름을 붙여 '용띠', '말띠'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: In Korea, people sometimes ask '무슨 띠예요?' (what's your zodiac animal?) as an indirect way to find out someone's age. People with the same animal differ in age by multiples of twelve years. You attach the animal name to '띠', as in '용띠' or '말띠'.

examples.en: I paid the toll at the tollgate and drove through.
Traffic backs up a lot in front of the tollgate.

examples.ko: 하이패스가 있으면 톨게이트를 서지 않고 통과해요.
examples.en: If you have a Hi-Pass, you pass through the tollgate without stopping.

examples.ko: 길을 잘 모르면 다음 톨게이트로 나가세요.
examples.en: If you're not sure of the way, exit at the next tollgate.
I check the navigation to see where the tollgate is.

examples.ko: 퇴근 시간에는 톨게이트 앞이 늘 복잡해요.
examples.en: During rush hour, the area before the tollgate is always crowded.

explain: 고속도로 요금을 받는 곳을 말해요. 공식적인 말로는 '요금소'라고 해요. '하이패스' 차선은 멈추지 않고 지나가는 곳이에요.
explain_en: It is the place on an expressway where tolls are collected. The more official term is '요금소'. A 'Hi-Pass' lane is one where you pass without stopping.

examples.en: I spent a night in a log cabin in the mountains with friends.
I like log cabins because they smell of wood.
We rented a log cabin and spent our summer vacation there.
Smoke is coming from the log cabin's chimney.
There is a small log cabin by the lake.

examples.ko: 통나무집에 가면 장작불을 피워 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: If I go to a log cabin, I want to try making a wood fire.

explain: 통나무로 지은 집이라서 산이나 호수 근처에서 놀러 갈 때 이야기하는 숙소로 많이 나와요. '통나무'는 가공하지 않은 굵은 나무 몸통이에요.
explain_en: Since it is a house built from logs, it often comes up as a place to stay on trips near mountains or lakes. '통나무' means an unprocessed thick tree trunk.

examples.ko: 귀화 후에는 투표권도 생겨서 선거에 참여할 수 있어요.
examples.en: After naturalization you also get the right to vote and can take part in elections.
You have the right to vote from age eighteen.

examples.ko: 투표권을 가진 사람만 투표할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people who hold the right to vote can vote.
There are elections in which foreigners have no right to vote.
Is there an age limit on the right to vote?
I brought my ID in order to exercise my right to vote.

explain: '선거권'과 비슷해서 바꿔 쓰기도 해요. 보통 '투표권을 행사하다'처럼 써요. 이때 '행사하다'는 '권리를 실제로 쓰다'라는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is similar to '선거권', and the two are sometimes interchanged. It is usually used as '투표권을 행사하다'. Here '행사하다' carries the feel of actually using a right.

examples.en: On election day they check your ID at the polling place.

examples.ko: 이사하면 투표는 어디서 해요? — 새 주소지 근처 투표소로 가면 돼요.
examples.en: Where do I vote if I move? — Just go to the polling place near your new address.
The polling place is close to my home, so I walked.

examples.ko: 투표소 앞에 사람들이 길게 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: People lined up in a long queue in front of the polling place.

examples.ko: 투표소는 아침 여섯 시에 문을 열어요.
examples.en: The polling place opens at six in the morning.

examples.ko: 투표소 안에서는 큰 소리로 이야기하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't talk loudly inside the polling place.

explain: 선거 날에 투표하는 장소예요. 학교나 주민센터가 투표소가 되는 경우가 많아요. 미리 투표하는 곳은 '사전투표소'라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It is the place where you vote on election day. Schools and community centers are often used as polling places. A place for early voting is called a '사전투표소' separately.

examples.ko: 투표일이 공휴일이라서 여행 가는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Voting day is a holiday, so some people go on trips.

examples.ko: 투표일 전에 후보들의 공약을 확인해 봤어요.
examples.en: Before voting day, I checked the candidates' pledges.
When is voting day for this election?

examples.ko: 투표일에 일이 있으면 미리 사전 투표를 하세요.
examples.en: If you have something on voting day, vote early in advance.
There aren't many days left until voting day.
I marked voting day on the calendar so I wouldn't forget.

explain: '선거일'과 거의 같은 날을 가리키지만, '사전 투표일'처럼 미리 투표하는 날을 따로 말할 때도 써요. '투표일'은 투표하는 날, '선거일'은 선거가 있는 날이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It points to nearly the same day as '선거일', but it is also used for separate voting days such as '사전 투표일' (early voting day). '투표일' feels like the day you vote, and '선거일' like the day the election takes place.

examples.ko: 한국식 치킨은 바삭한 튀김옷과 달콤한 양념이 특징이에요.
examples.en: Korean fried chicken is known for its crispy batter and sweet sauce.
I coat the shrimp in batter and fry it in oil.
If the batter is too thick, it tastes greasy.
You make the batter by mixing the flour into cold water.

examples.ko: 튀김옷 때문에 고기 맛이 잘 안 느껴져요.
examples.en: Because of the batter, I can't taste the meat well.

examples.ko: 튀김옷에 빵가루를 한 번 더 묻혀 보세요.
examples.en: Try coating it with breadcrumbs one more time over the batter.

explain: 음식에 옷을 입히는 것처럼 반죽을 묻힌다고 봐서 '튀김옷을 입히다'라고 말해요. '옷'이 들어간 말이지만 먹을 수 있는 부분이에요.
explain_en: Because coating the food is likened to dressing it, you say '튀김옷을 입히다'. Although it contains the word 'clothes' (옷), it is the edible coating.

examples.en: I memorize Korean words whenever I have a spare moment.
I know you're busy, but come visit when you get a chance.

examples.ko: 요즘은 틈날 때마다 공원에서 산책을 해요.
examples.en: These days I take a walk in the park whenever I have time.
I found a free moment at lunchtime and took a short nap.
Rest even briefly when you get a free moment.
After the meeting ends, I'll call you as soon as I get a free moment.

explain: '시간이 나다'와 비슷하지만, 바쁜 중에 잠깐 생긴 짧은 시간이라는 느낌이 강해요. '틈나는 대로', '틈날 때마다'처럼 자주 쓰고, '틈이 나다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '시간이 나다' but strongly suggests a short gap in an otherwise busy schedule. It is common in '틈나는 대로' and '틈날 때마다', and you can also say '틈이 나다'.

examples.ko: 커피에 티스푼으로 설탕을 두 번 넣어요.
examples.en: I add sugar to my coffee with a teaspoon, twice.
Sorry, but could you give me one more teaspoon?

examples.ko: 카레 가루는 티스푼으로 한 번만 넣으세요.
examples.en: Add the curry powder with a teaspoon, just once.
The teaspoon is small, so it's inconvenient for eating soup.

examples.ko: 티스푼은 서랍 두 번째 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The teaspoons are in the second drawer.
I scooped honey onto a teaspoon and put it in the tea.

explain: 작은 숟가락은 '티스푼' 말고 '찻숟가락'이라고도 해요. 한국 요리책에서 양을 말할 때는 '작은술'(티스푼 한 숟가락)과 '큰술'을 써요.
explain_en: A small spoon can also be called '찻숟가락' instead of '티스푼'. In Korean recipes, amounts are written as '작은술' (one teaspoon) and '큰술' (one tablespoon).

examples.en: After playing in the winter sea, my lips turned blue.
In autumn the sky is clear, so it gets bluer.
I saw his face turn pale blue from shock.
I played in the pool until my lips turned blue.

examples.ko: 물감을 더 넣으면 색이 파래질 거예요.
examples.en: If you add more paint, the color will turn bluer.

examples.ko: 오래 밖에 있었더니 손가락이 파래지고 아팠어요.
examples.en: After being outside for a long time, my fingers turned blue and hurt.

explain: '파랗다'에 '-아지다'가 붙은 말이라 '파래져요'로 활용해요. 추위나 놀람 때문에 입술·얼굴이 파랗게 변할 때 자주 쓰고, 놀라서 얼굴색이 변하는 건 '파랗게 질리다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is '파랗다' plus '-아지다', so it conjugates as '파래져요'. It is often used when lips or a face turn blue from cold or shock, and a face going pale from fright can also be described with '파랗게 질리다'.

examples.en: Your new perm suits you well.
I got a perm at the hair salon yesterday.
Permed hair looks prettier when you wet it.
I have permed hair, so it's easy to style in the morning.
Since I changed to permed hair, my overall look has changed.

examples.ko: 저기 짧은 파마머리 아주머니가 우리 이모예요.
examples.en: The woman with short permed hair over there is my aunt.

explain: 파마로 만든 곱슬한 머리를 말해요. 타고난 곱슬은 '곱슬머리', 파마를 안 한 곧은 머리는 '생머리'라고 해서 구분해요. 보통 '파마를 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It means curly hair made with a perm. Naturally curly hair is '곱슬머리' and straight hair without a perm is '생머리'. People usually say '파마를 하다' for getting a perm.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 동네 형과 팔씨름 대결을 한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I once had an arm-wrestling match with an older boy from the neighborhood.
In arm wrestling, wrist strength is important.
We arm wrestled for a bet and I lost.
I want to beat my father at arm wrestling.

examples.ko: 점심 내기로 팔씨름 한 판 할래요?
examples.en: Want to arm wrestle once for lunch?
As soon as the arm wrestling ended, my arm was tingling.

explain: '팔씨름을 하다'라고 하고, 한 번 겨루는 건 '한 판'으로 세요. '씨름'은 한국 전통 레슬링인데, '팔씨름'은 팔만으로 힘을 겨루는 놀이예요.
explain_en: You say '팔씨름을 하다', and one round is counted as '한 판'. '씨름' is traditional Korean wrestling, while '팔씨름' is a contest of strength using just the arm.

examples.ko: 동지에는 팥죽을 먹는 풍습이 지금도 있어요.
examples.en: The custom of eating red bean porridge on the winter solstice still exists today.

examples.ko: 팥죽에 설탕을 넣어서 먹는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people add sugar to their red bean porridge.
Red bean porridge tastes best when eaten warm.
I miss the red bean porridge my grandmother used to cook.

examples.ko: 팥죽 한 그릇 먹고 나니 몸이 따뜻해졌어요.
examples.en: After a bowl of red bean porridge, my body warmed up.
I'm going to have red bean porridge for lunch today.

explain: 팥으로 쑨 죽이고, 동지에 먹는 음식으로 유명해요. 붉은 팥이 나쁜 기운을 쫓는다고 믿었기 때문이에요. 죽은 '쑤다'라는 동사를 써서 '팥죽을 쑤다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is porridge made from red beans and is famous as a food eaten on the winter solstice, because red beans were believed to drive away bad luck. For porridge you can use the verb '쑤다', as in '팥죽을 쑤다' (to cook red bean porridge).

examples.en: The spot where I bumped turned a deep bluish bruise.
I got a blue bruise on my knee.
The mold was bluish-green, so I threw the bread away.

examples.ko: 멍 색이 이제 덜 퍼레 보여요.
examples.en: The bruise looks less blue now.
The deep blue bruise turned yellow after a few days.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 입술이 퍼레요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day, and my lips are blue.

explain: '파랗다'보다 짙고 탁한 파란색이에요. 그래서 멍이나 추위로 변한 입술처럼 좋지 않은 느낌에 자주 써요. '시퍼렇다'는 더 강한 말이고, 활용은 '퍼레요'처럼 ㅎ이 빠져요.
explain_en: It is a deeper, duller blue than '파랗다', so it is often used for unpleasant things like bruises or lips discolored by cold. '시퍼렇다' is the stronger form, and it conjugates by dropping ㅎ, as in '퍼레요'.

examples.en: I painted the old wardrobe.
I can see a house painted white in the distance.
The paint is peeling, so I have to redo it.
Painting the wall takes just two days.

examples.ko: 페인트칠 하는 동안 창문을 열어 두세요.
examples.en: Keep the windows open while painting.
Can you lend me a brush to use for painting?

explain: '페인트를 칠하다'와 같은 뜻이고, '페인트칠을 하다'로도 말해요. 벽에 벽지를 붙이는 일은 '도배'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '페인트를 칠하다' and can also be said as '페인트칠을 하다'. Putting wallpaper on walls is called '도배', which is a different job.

examples.ko: 다 마신 페트병은 재활용 통에 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please put empty plastic bottles in the recycling bin.

examples.ko: 페트병도 재활용이 돼요? — 네, 라벨을 떼고 버리세요.
examples.en: Can plastic bottles be recycled too? — Yes, remove the label and throw it away.
I filled a plastic bottle with water and put it in the freezer.
I flatten plastic bottles before throwing them away.
I made a flowerpot out of an empty plastic bottle.
Plastic bottles are light, so they're easy to carry.

explain: 물이나 음료가 담긴 투명한 플라스틱 병을 말해요. 한국에서는 분리배출할 때 라벨을 떼고 헹궈서 버리라고 안내해요. '병' 앞에 붙여 쓰는 한 단어예요.
explain_en: It means the clear plastic bottles that hold water or drinks. In Korea, recycling guides tell you to remove the label and rinse it before disposal. It is written as one word, attached to '병'.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 편리성이 가장 큰 장점이에요.
examples.en: This app's biggest strength is its convenience.
If you only consider convenience, a card is better than cash.
I think convenience is more important than price.

examples.ko: 온라인 쇼핑의 편리성 덕분에 시장에 잘 안 가요.
examples.en: Thanks to the convenience of online shopping, I rarely go to the market.
The convenience is good, but the price is too high.
You have to take care of both convenience and safety.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '편해요'나 '편리해요'라고 말하고, '편리성'은 제품이나 서비스를 비교하거나 설명할 때 써요. '-성'이 붙은 말이라 '안전성', '효율성'과 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people say '편해요' or '편리해요', while '편리성' is used when comparing or describing products and services. It ends in '-성', so it often appears alongside words like '안전성' (safety) and '효율성' (efficiency).
